papers.title_en: Back to Raw Motion: Latent-Free Diffusion Transformers for Text-to-Motion and Exact Conditional Generation
papers.authors: Yun Chen, Jeonghyeok Do, Munchurl Kim
papers.evidence: 面向原始运动空间文本驱动动作生成的无潜变量扩散Transformer
papers.tldr: 该文指出现有生成模型依赖学习到的编解码器压缩潜变量，可能丢失细节且无法精确保持给定条件。作者借鉴图像像素扩散，将文本驱动动作生成引入原始运动空间，提出RawMo无潜变量扩散Transformer框架，直接在原始动作数据上建模。初步研究显示该方法可在实用计算成本下生成高质量动作并精确保持条件，为3D人体动作生成提供了绕开编解码器的新范式。
papers.abstract_en: As generative models tackle larger and more complex datasets, learned codecs enable efficient generation through compact latent representations, but may lose details and cannot guarantee exact preservation of given conditions. Generating directly in the original data space avoids errors introduced by the codec. Recent advances in image generation demonstrate that pixel diffusion can produce high-quality samples at practical computational costs. Inspired by these advances, we conduct a preliminary study of pixel diffusion, demonstrating its potential for adaptation to motion generation. Building on these findings, we present RawMo, a framework that brings text-to-motion generation to raw motion space. Our Motion Diffusion Transformer (MiT) models local skeletal structures and whole-body dynamics, while refining motion across frames to improve temporal consistency. Working directly in raw motion space further allows our high-noise text-motion alignment loss (HiNCE) to improve text consistency without intermediate motion decoding. RawMo supports multiple motion-conditioning tasks with a single conditional model while preserving given motion conditions exactly. Experiments on HumanML3D and KIT-ML show the best text alignment among compared methods and competitive motion quality, with ablations confirming the benefits of MiT and HiNCE.

papers.title_en: MMotion: Collaborative Cross-Scale Memory for Text-to-Motion Generation
papers.authors: Zhaoxin Fan, Qingchen Yu, Kejian Wu, Jian Yang, Zeming Liu, wenjun wu, Lili Wang
papers.evidence: 文本到动作生成逼真人体动作序列
papers.tldr: 针对现有文本到动作方法要么检索动作样例、要么保留长程上下文，却很少利用记忆联合推理语义、动态与生成历史的问题，本文提出MMotion协作式多尺度记忆框架。语义记忆在不同生成尺度提供动作先验，动态记忆捕捉潜在状态转移，工作记忆保留已生成内容的因果上下文。该框架统一三类记忆生成逼真的人体动作序列，为文本驱动3D动作生成提供了新思路。
papers.abstract_en: Text-to-motion generation aims to synthesize realistic human motions from natural-language descriptions, enabling applications in animation, virtual avatars, and embodied agents. Despite recent progress, existing methods either retrieve motion exemplars or retain long-range context, but rarely exploit memory to jointly reason about semantics, dynamics, and generation history. In this paper, we propose MMotion, a collaborative multi-scale memory framework that unifies scale-conditioned semantic retrieval, latent dynamics modeling, and causal working memory. Specifically, semantic memory provides motion priors at different generation scales, dynamics memory captures latent state transitions, and working memory preserves causal context from previously generated motions. A collaborative fusion mechanism integrates these complementary memories to determine what motion to generate, how it should evolve, and how it should remain consistent with its history. MMotion is architecture-agnostic and can be readily integrated into both diffusion-based and next scale autoregressive models. Extensive experiments across standard benchmarks and diverse backbones demonstrate consistent improvements over strong baselines.

papers.title_en: MotionODE: Enhancing Autoregressive Text-to-Motion Generation with Continuous-Depth Modeling
papers.authors: Zhaoxin Fan, Jian Yang, Kejian Wu, Zeming Liu, Wenjun Wu, Lili Wang
papers.evidence: 用连续深度ODE建模改进自回归文本驱动动作生成
papers.tldr: 该文针对自回归文本驱动动作生成中局部预测需协调跨时文本与动作上下文的问题，指出条件动作表示的内在形成少有探索。作者提出MotionODE连续深度后训练框架，将选定Transformer残差分支视为局部向量场并用中点Runge-Kutta积分替换更新，保持表示与生成机制不变。方法缓解了条件与上下文不匹配问题，为基于连续深度/流式建模的动作生成提供了可迁移思路。
papers.abstract_en: Autoregressive text-to-motion generation requires local motion predictions to reconcile cross-temporal textual requirements with the available motion context. While existing methods primarily improve motion representations and generation order, the internal formation of conditioned motion representations remains less explored. We introduce MotionODE, a continuous-depth post-training framework that refines hidden-state evolution in pretrained autoregressive generators. MotionODE reinterprets selected Transformer residual branches as local vector fields and replaces their original updates with midpoint Runge--Kutta (RK2) integration, while preserving the motion representation and outer generation mechanism. To address the mismatch between pretrained update paths and newly introduced intermediate states, we propose mixed one-step/two-step RK2 post-training under motion-token supervision, with optional distillation and update-map constraints to preserve pretrained behavior. This minimally invasive framework supports both next-token and next-scale generation without training the generator from scratch. Extensive experiments on HumanML3D demonstrate consistent improvements in text--motion alignment across MoScale, BAMM and LMR, highlighting internal representation updates as a complementary direction for improving autoregressive motion generation.

papers.title_en: ContextHands: Completing Hand Motion with Learned Context and Joint-Specific Body Kinematics
papers.authors: Taewoo Kim, Seunghun Koh, Hyosup Shin, Sungho Jo
papers.evidence: 扩散生成器由身体与语言补全3D手部动作
papers.tldr: 针对生成人体动作中手部细节不足、难以从身体动作与语言推断手部关节的问题，本文提出ContextHands方法，从观测到的身体序列与文本描述补全手部动作。方法学习概率化手部特征，并利用辅助手部预测连接这些特征与手部关节，身体编码器在多时间尺度上保留关节与身体部位信息供手部查询。扩散生成器据此合成细致的手部动作，提升了生成人体动作的真实感与表现力。
papers.abstract_en: Detailed hand motion contributes to the realism and expressiveness of generated human motion. Completing these details from body motion and language requires connecting the context of an action to the articulation of the hands. We introduce ContextHands, which completes hand motion from an observed body sequence and text descriptions assigned to hands and time intervals. Our approach learns probabilistic hand features from the descriptions and body motion, using auxiliary hand prediction to connect these features to hand articulation. A body encoder preserves joint and body-part features across multiple temporal scales, allowing each hand joint to query these features for joint-specific body information. The diffusion generator combines this joint-specific body information with the learned hand context. Both encoders and the generator are trained jointly, so the final generation objective also shapes the context features. Experiments on the OakInk2 dataset show that ContextHands generates more accurate hand motion and achieves lower Fréchet Hand Distance than existing hand-motion and general human-motion generation methods adapted to the task. In qualitative examples of grasping and tool use, ContextHands more closely reproduces the detailed hand poses in the reference motion. We will release our code and pretrained models to support further research.

papers.title_en: SemPhys: Semantic-Physical Co-Learning for Humanoid Motion Generation via Differentiable World Models
papers.authors: Zejian Kang, Yeqiang Wang, Zekai Chen, Boyang Shen, Mingyu Ma, Bingqian Wu, Fan Zhou, Jianjie Zhang, Chentao Shen, Wentao Yang, Rui Qian, Xiangru Huang
papers.evidence: 通过可微世界模型生成人形全身动作
papers.tldr: 针对语言指令生成的运动学参考经跟踪控制器执行后会偏离、从而改变动作语义的问题，本文提出SemPhys框架。其核心思想是直接在机器人实际执行的完整动作上评估语义对齐，利用可微世界模型从仿真执行中获取语义反馈来训练动作生成器。该方法使生成动作在满足物理平衡约束的同时保持与指令语义一致，提升了人形动作生成在真实执行中的可靠性。
papers.abstract_en: In human-robot collaboration, natural language lets people direct a humanoid's whole-body movements without programming joint trajectories. A common approach generates a kinematic reference from an instruction and relies on a tracking controller to execute it. However, as the controller maintains balance under contact constraints, the executed motion can depart from the reference in ways that change the action it conveys. Our central insight is that semantic alignment must be evaluated directly on the complete motion the robot physically executes. Building on this insight, we introduce \textbf{SemPhys}, a framework that trains motion generators using semantic feedback from simulated executions. A differentiable world model and a fixed tracking controller predict a short segment of a recorded execution. SemPhys inserts this prediction at its original position, scores the complete trajectory against the instruction, and backpropagates through the predicted segment. A paired anchoring loss stabilizes adaptation by keeping each generated reference close to its counterpart from the initial generator. On BONES-SEED, SemPhys largely preserves instruction retrieval accuracy from reference to execution and achieves the highest retrieval accuracy on executed motions among the evaluated methods.

papers.title_en: MoSk: A Unified Motion-Skeleton Foundation Model for Human Motion Understanding and Generation
papers.authors: Yun Chen, Munchurl Kim, Jeonghyeok Do
papers.evidence: 人体动作理解与生成的基础模型
papers.tldr: 针对人体动作领域基础模型尚未充分探索的问题，作者提出MoSk，这是首个将大规模动作数据集与骨架数据集融合的运动-骨架基础模型。模型通过自监督方式学习共享表征，兼顾动作理解与生成能力。实验在动作识别等理解任务和生成任务上验证了融合两类数据的有效性。该工作为人体动作的统一建模提供了新的基础模型范式。
papers.abstract_en: Foundation models (FMs) have advanced visual understanding and generation by providing semantically rich representations. However, this role of FMs remains underexplored in human motion. Large motion datasets offer diverse movements at scale, but often lack action labels for systematically evaluating learned representations on understanding tasks. Skeleton datasets enable such evaluation through established recognition protocols, yet are typically smaller and focus on predefined actions captured in controlled environments. To combine these strengths, we present MoSk, to the best of our knowledge, the first Motion-Skeleton foundation model to integrate motion and skeleton datasets. MoSk learns shared representations through self-supervised masked motion modeling. We incorporate joint-name embeddings to provide a common anatomical reference across various skeleton formats. A cross-attention decoder reconstructs masked motion from the encoder's features, with joint-name embeddings specifying the target joints. Experiments demonstrate strong action-recognition performance across diverse settings, including linear evaluation and fine-tuning. MoSk also substantially improves motion generation across multiple backbones through representation alignment, reducing FID on MotionMillion by up to 9.75 for unconditional generation and 3.83 for text-to-motion generation.

papers.title_en: AGLR: Attribute-Guided Latent Refinement for Fine-Grained Humanoid Motion Generation and Editing
papers.authors: Shuai Yuan, Yuwei Gui, Mingshuang Luo, Zhuo Li, Siyuan Meng, Wenhao Cui, RuiBing Hou, Bingpeng Ma
papers.evidence: 细粒度人形3D动作生成与编辑
papers.tldr: 针对语言控制缺乏几何精度、关节级约束欠定导致难以同时满足目标与保留源动作的问题，本文提出属性引导的潜在细化框架AGLR，通过源锚定的细化方式对生成或已有的人形动作进行局部编辑。方法提供紧凑的几何接口，支持对肢体伸展、躯干朝向与根轨迹进行可组合、时变的控制。实验表明该方法能在满足新几何约束的同时较好保留原始动作细节，为细粒度人形动作生成与编辑提供了统一方案。
papers.abstract_en: Humanoid motion generation must accommodate evolving task requirements, where localized adjustments should satisfy new geometric constraints without disrupting desired motion details. However, language-based control lacks geometric precision, while joint-level constraints require explicit spatial targets. Local geometric constraints are also underdetermined, complicating target satisfaction and source preservation. We present AGLR (Attribute-Guided Latent Refinement), a unified framework for fine-grained humanoid motion generation and editing through source-anchored refinement. A compact geometric interface supports composable, time-varying control of limb extents, torso orientation, and root trajectories. Given a generated or encoded base latent, an Attribute Residual Adapter predicts a single-pass correction, with dual-level supervision enforcing target matching and selective preservation across attributes and motion coordinates. On HumanML3D-G1, AGLR achieves the highest controllable-generation and preservation-constrained editing success rates among evaluated methods. Editing take only 9.1 ms for a cached 500-frame motion, without additional sampling or test-time optimization. Zero-shot evaluation on BONES-SEED-G1 further demonstrates transfer without fine-tuning.
